blocks.text: David’s response to Saul and Jonathan’s deaths is public mourning rather than celebration. His lament honors their courage, remembers Saul’s benefits to Israel, and speaks personally of Jonathan’s love. By ordering the song to be taught in Judah, David gives this grief a continuing public place.

This opening chapter stands at the beginning of a book that follows David’s rise and consolidation as king, then moves through the ark and dynasty promise, royal wrongdoing, violence within his household, rebellion, grief, and a closing appendix. The lament begins that larger story with loss and public remembrance.
